title: Conversion preserves communication complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic finite-message two-party protocol with input types $X$ and $Y$ and output type $\alpha$, where each message is drawn from a finite nonempty type. The binary protocol obtained by converting $p$ has the same communication complexity as $p$.
hypotheses_covered: $p$ is a finite-message protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$ with output type $\alpha$
Each message type used by $p$ is finite and nonempty
replaced:
Let $p$ be a finite-message deterministic two-party communication protocol over input
types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with outputs in $\alpha$, in which each message is an
element of an arbitrary finite nonempty type. Its conversion into a binary protocol,
obtained by encoding every $\beta$-valued message as $\lceil \log_2 \abs{\beta} \rceil$
bits, has communication complexity equal to that of $p$.
